trigger: operator live report (not yet a GitHub issue at trigger time): reloading sort's page mid-run, then starting a new run, causes 'weird effects'
verification: Reproduction attempted extensively via Playwright against the live site: reference-sorter (bridge-local handler) completes a full run in ~1.5-2s wall-clock (measured), too fast to catch mid-flight via any realistic reload timing -- confirmed clean state on every post-reload run. Attempted the same against the two live channel participants (tobi, bennet) for a longer window; discovered BOTH were independently stuck in a real, pre-existing (not caused by this session) failure: PersistentRoleClient labels 3588bf28 (tobi) and b688e09b (bennet) were cycling 30s-timeout/kill/respawn continuously, tobi's for 2.5+ hours. While tracing this live via docker logs, found the actual root cause by reading _callOnce/_spawn: _kill()'s SIGKILL is asynchronous relative to call()'s own catch-and-retry, so a killed child's 'close' event can arrive AFTER a retry has already spawned a fresh child and moved this.pendingResolve on to it -- with no per-call child identity tracking, that stale close incorrectly settles (rejects) the WRONG (newer, possibly-succeeding) call using the dead child's exit reason. This explains the repeated 30s cascades directly (each retry gets spuriously killed by the previous attempt's late close, forcing yet another cycle) and is a real, confirmed, general PersistentRoleClient bug, not confined to reload.
rollback: sort-demo-bridge:sort40-key-leak-fix (pre-fix) if ever needed, but reintroduces the confirmed spurious-rejection bug
note: FIX: added this.pendingResolveChild tracking which child a given pendingResolve callback actually belongs to; the close/error handlers in _spawn() and the stdin-write-error path in _callOnce() now only settle the pending call if the closing/erroring child matches pendingResolveChild, otherwise the event is correctly treated as stale and ignored. New regression test in waiting-room.test.js drives this through the real public call() API (a hung first attempt timing out, a fast-answering retry) and asserts the retry's real answer wins -- removing the fix (git stash) made this exact test hang rather than fail cleanly, itself supporting that real, meaningful behavior changed. Full suite 91/91 green. Deployed: image rebuilt, container recreated (not restarted), /healthz 200 live, fix confirmed present in the running container's own /app/server.js (grep pendingResolveChild -> 12 hits). NOT CONFIRMED: whether this specific bug is THE mechanism behind the operator's original 'weird effects on reload+new-run' report -- could not obtain a clean, unconfounded live reproduction of that exact report (both available channel participants were independently broken for unrelated reasons during the investigation window, and the fast bridge-local baseline finishes before a reload can ever land mid-stream). Filed as a GitHub issue with full detail rather than closing anything on an unconfirmed mechanism; this fix ships because it is independently real and correct, and cross-referenced against sort#25 since it also explains part of that issue's own 60-80s cascade pattern.
